guards.note: clean: validate() first calls strip_link_attachments(self.tree), removing every //link[@rel="attachment"] element from the shared document tree; reached from PdfWriter.pdf -> PrepToolWriter.prep -> dispatch('.;validate_before()') -> validate_before -> PrepToolWriter.validate -> BaseV3Writer.validate. Regressed: no such call, the element survives
added by the fix: xpath //link[@rel="attachment"] and remove each from its parent

sinks.note: HtmlWriter.html() renders the (unprepped-input, now prepped) tree; HtmlWriter.render_rfc moves each <rfc>/<link> element verbatim into the HTML <head>; the HTML string goes to weasyprint.HTML(string=html, base_url="").write_pdf(...), and WeasyPrint's default URL fetcher opens the href of <link rel="attachment"> from the local filesystem and embeds the file in the output PDF (the open() itself is inside the WeasyPrint library)

notes: Written at 2.3 (2026-09-29). Class: path-traversal (CWE-22 per advisory); by behaviour an attacker-controlled local file path (href of <link rel="attachment">) is opened and its contents embedded in the output PDF, i.e. arbitrary file read via external control of a filename. KNOWN-INCOMPLETE FIX: the clean commit strips attachments only inside BaseV3Writer.validate, which runs only when the preptool runs; PdfWriter.pdf and HtmlWriter.html_tree skip the preptool when the input already carries prepTime, so prepped input still reaches WeasyPrint with the attachment link. That bypass is GHSA-9mv7-3c64-mmqw / CVE-2025-11059, fixed by 73fb1c91 (event xml2rfc-9mv7). The modelled flow is the one this commit does close: UNPREPPED input (no prepTime) -> PdfWriter.pdf -> PrepToolWriter.prep -> BaseV3Writer.dispatch runs selector '.;validate_before()' (method name built by slugify, called via getattr) -> BaseV3Writer.validate_before -> PrepToolWriter.validate -> BaseV3Writer.validate [clean: strip_link_attachments(self.tree)] -> back in PdfWriter.pdf, HtmlWriter(self.xmlrfc).html() -> html_tree (prepTime now set on the shared tree, so no second prep) -> render -> render_rfc, which moves every <rfc>/<link> element verbatim into the HTML <head> (head.append(link)) -> html string -> flatten_unicode_spans -> weasyprint.HTML(string=html, base_url='').write_pdf(...), where WeasyPrint's default URL fetcher opens the attachment href. The prep tool mutates xmlrfc.tree in place (xinclude and dispatch act on self.tree = xmlrfc.tree), so the strip is visible to the HtmlWriter. The earlier reviewers named HtmlWriter.render_link as the copy point; at b4f349fa the <rfc>-level links (the only place the v3 schema allows <link>) are moved by render_rfc before children are rendered, so render_link is not on this path and is left out. Dynamic dispatch hops (dispatch -> validate_before via getattr on a selector string; render -> render_rfc via getattr('render_%s')) will not be resolved by a plain call graph. The actual file open is inside the third-party WeasyPrint library (write_pdf), not in the repo; taint tools need write_pdf/weasyprint.HTML modelled as a filesystem sink. Entry: the parsed input document enters the writers through BaseV3Writer.__init__ (self.tree = xmlrfc.tree); the real parse is XmlRfcParser.parse in parser.py (large, called from run.py main), recorded as true_symbol. Guard: BaseV3Writer.validate (call site) plus the new utils.strip_link_attachments; strip_link_attachments exists only at the clean commit. Parallel flow closed by the same change but not modelled: HtmlWriter.write/html_tree on unprepped input (HTML output, no file read by xml2rfc itself). Size: clean slice ~40.8 KB, over the 24 KB soft limit but under the hard limit; about 22 KB is html.py, almost all of it HtmlWriter.render_rfc (the hop that copies <link> into the HTML head, ~290 lines mostly RFC 7992 spec comments) plus the renderer aliases the builder keeps as class-level assignments. render_rfc cannot be cut without removing a hop; page_css_template (page stylesheet text) was cut. Accepted dropped references: html.py add/build (lxml ElementMaker wrappers that build HTML nodes; the tainted <link> is moved with head.append, not built by them), seen, read_css, post_process; pdf.py get_serif_fonts/get_mono_fonts/page_css_template (fonts and page CSS); base.py schema/tag constants, default_options, RfcWriterError, logging helpers (die/warn/note/log), deadly_error, check_includes, get_all_attribute_defaults, validate_draft_name; utils.py namespaces and find_duplicate_attr_values (schema ID duplicate check). None is on the link-to-file flow. The slice is not importable as-is (default_options default argument, render_contact = render_author alias).
